placements.why: This envelope's entire content — a database technology migration, its performance/cost rationale, and its timeline — is an infrastructure/technical-architecture decision. No strata exists yet in this repo; Architecture is the canonical organizational category (from the ratified Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates/Calibration taxonomy) this content calls for, and nothing closer is available to relate it to, so it mints standalone with no parent.
placements.title: Technical infrastructure decisions as an organizational category
placements.frame: Does this content name a system, platform, or infrastructure choice the organization is making or has made — the kind of decision future envelopes will keep reporting on as it plays out?

placements.title: Technical decisions arrive pre-ratified, not proposed
placements.frame: Is this technical/infrastructure change being performed as already underway or settled — via present-continuous verbs, arrow notation, or fixed deadlines — rather than opened for input or review?
placements.why: src-1's present-continuous 'We're switching', src-3's bolded arrow notation recording the migration as fact, and src-5's bolded fixed 'Q3 2026' deadline all perform the database migration as a settled decision rather than a proposal — a pattern of unilateral technical decision-making that future envelopes reporting on this org's engineering decisions will keep feeding. This is a recurring organizational behavior (how decisions get made), not a one-time fact, so it clears the narrative grain test; it names the same subject the conviction/relational/power dimensional reads independently converged on (decision region, authority-ranking, informational/pressure) and aligns with the position pass's DecisionRatificationFraming grouping.

placements.title: Quantified benefit figures stand in for verified evidence
placements.frame: Are the performance and cost figures offered to justify this technical decision flat, unhedged assertions, or are they independently substantiated — and does that pattern recur across the org's technical decisions?
placements.why: src-2 ('10x query performance, lower licensing cost') and src-4 ('10x analytical queries') both restate the same quantified performance/cost claims as flat, unhedged assertions offered to justify the migration — a recurring pattern of how this org builds its technical-decision case (evidence style), distinct from the decision-ratification act itself. This names a subject — how quantified claims function as justification — that future envelopes will keep feeding, not a one-time statistic; it tracks the conviction pass's 'claim' region and the position pass's PerformanceCostJustification grouping.
